storyboardBeats.narration: Pull your transmission dipstick. This ten-second look is worth checking.
storyboardBeats.providerScene: Extreme macro, a transmission dipstick suspended just above a white inspection cloth as if rig-mounted, a bead of bright red fluid catching the light, shallow depth of field, slow push-in, warm garage practical lighting, cinematic automotive commercial look, 9:16 vertical framing, no hand visible

storyboardBeats.narration: Bright red and clear usually means it's doing its job.
storyboardBeats.providerScene: Close-up of a single fluid droplet on white cloth, vivid translucent red, soft diffused key light, slow rack focus, texture-forward, 9:16 vertical framing

storyboardBeats.narration: Brown, black, or a burnt smell can point to fluid breaking down.
storyboardBeats.providerScene: Side-by-side macro comparison of two fluid swatches on white cloth — one bright red, one dark brown/black — even overhead light, slow lateral pan across the two swatches, 9:16 vertical framing

storyboardBeats.narration: That's one clue — don't guess. It could mean a transmission already wearing itself out.
storyboardBeats.providerScene: Macro shot of a transmission pan and underside components in a garage bay, dim practical lighting shifting to a harsher amber tone, slow dolly across metal surfaces, texture-forward, 9:16 vertical framing

storyboardBeats.narration: Send this to someone who hasn't checked theirs in years. Stop by and we'll take a look — Nick's Tire and Auto, link in bio.
